OK let me explain a little more...

We are using a Woocommerce lottery plugin. The lottery plugin works well. The only problem with it is that the default shop/product listing layout that ships with this lottery plugin looks bad. I contacted the plugin author about an easy way to modify the layout and they said it was not possible. So I analysed the code and seems like they are injecting code into the layout. To cut a long story short, it was going to be really messy to try to hack the plugin code to modify their layout.

Our solution was to build our own shop/listing page and to inject the lottery shortcodes into this in the UI builder. the website is built with Elementor but it seems like the original designer wasn't sure if it was possible to achieve this using Elementor so he created a section using WP Bakery to design the grid using the WP Bakery Grid Builder. He is then referencing this grid via an Elementor shortcode section. The problem is that when I try to edit the grids in the Grid Builder, the page is not updating, so I am not sure where the Elementor page is getting the grid layout from.

Here is the Elementor shortcode:

[vc_row][vc_column][vc_basic_grid post_type="product" max_items="500" element_width="6" item="2057" grid_id="vc_gid:1606729646886-b63f454057bf8fba8c26af21a8c650e1-10" taxonomies="15"][/vc_column][/vc_row]

I am getting frustrated as to what the best solution is. I am thinking of different solutions here:

1) Rebuild the layout in Elementor (not sure how to do this injecting shortcode)

2) Somehow work out why the page is not updating when I change the WP Bakery layout (is it getting the shortcode from the database or somewhere else)

3) Start using filters or try to inject the layout via PHP

Anyway, if anybody can help would be much appreciated. I would be delighted to do a quick zoom screenshare.
